opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kathryn Bishop (employee ID E023) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E023.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Kathryn Bishop (E023) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; write is at the maximum for this role, so recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E023 is a contractor with basic training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; requested write exceeds this, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes conflict on Kathryn Bishop's (E023) employment status: HR states full-time, while Security states contractor with basic training. If full-time, write would be within policy (max write, since Engineer does not own Payroll). However, Security's records indicate contractor with basic training, which caps the maximum at read. Given the unresolved contradiction, the safe/least-privilege decision is to grant read, which is within policy under either reading of the more restrictive facts and never exceeds the requested write level.
